bullets: How the roots, stem and leaves work together, and why plants do not eat food from the soil
slides.heading: Plant systems
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we tour the plant system - the roots hold the plant and drink, the stem lifts it and carries water up, and the leaves make its food.

bullets: Follow water on its journey from the roots up the stem to the leaves
Watch the leaves catch sunlight and make food for the plant
Explain why plants do not take food from the soil through their roots
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the three goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to trace the water journey and spot the mistake about plants eating from the soil.

bullets: A pupil says plants take food from the soil through their roots, like we eat food
Do the roots really eat, or do they only drink?
slides.heading: Do plants eat food from the soil?
slides.notes: Pose the claim from scene s4 without the verdict first: ask for a show of hands on whether roots eat food from the soil, take two or three answers without judging them, and say scene s3 and scene s4 settle this exactly.

bullets: Each part of the plant has its own job, and the parts work together as a system
The leaves make the food: roots drink water and minerals, and the stem carries the water up to the leaves
slides.heading: Each plant part has its own job
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the roots and stem deliver water, and the leaves use that water with sunlight to make the food for the whole plant.

bullets: The roots grow down into the soil and hold the plant in place
The roots drink up water from the soil for the whole plant
slides.heading: Roots: the plant holds on and drinks
slides.notes: Narrate the roots growing down into the soil, watch them hold the plant steady, then follow the water as the roots drink it up for the whole plant.

bullets: The stem holds the plant up so the leaves can reach the light
Water travels up the stem from the roots to the leaves, like traffic on a road
slides.heading: Stem: the plant's lift and road
slides.notes: Follow a drop of water as it travels up the stem from the roots, and point out how the stem also holds the plant up so the leaves can reach the light.

bullets: The leaves catch sunlight
With sunlight and water, the leaves make food for the plant - the plant does not eat food like we do
slides.heading: Leaves: the plant makes its own food
slides.notes: Watch the leaves catch the sunlight, then show how they use the sunlight together with the water from the roots to make food for the plant.

bullets: The roots look like a mouth, but they are not: roots drink water and minerals, they do not eat
The leaves make the food with sunlight, so the plant takes no food from the soil
slides.heading: Watch out: plants do not eat food from the soil
slides.notes: Hold the mistake up first - plants take food from the soil through their roots - then watch what the roots really drink and what the leaves make, which proves the plant does not eat food from the soil.

bullets: Follow one drop: the roots drink it, the stem carries it up, and the leaves use it to make food
Each stop on the journey is a different plant part doing its own job
slides.heading: Worked example: trace one drop of water
slides.notes: Talk through the journey in scenes s1 to s3 slowly and name each step: the roots drink the drop, the stem carries it up, and the leaves use it with sunlight to make food.

bullets: Put the water journey in order: roots, stem, leaves - what happens at each stop?
Explain to your partner why plants do not eat food from the soil, using the word leaves in your answer
slides.heading: Your turn: explain the plant system
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them to name the plant parts in order and to use the leaves making food as their evidence.

bullets: On your own: draw a plant and label the roots, stem and leaves
Explain in one sentence what the roots really take from the soil
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for all three parts labelled, plus one clear sentence about roots drinking water and minerals, not eating food.
